title: Making Audiences Laugh Is a Serious Creative Exercise: Anil Ravipudi at IFFI 2026
content:
Goa, 25 November 2026
“Making audiences laugh is a demanding creative exercise”, said National Film Award-winning filmmaker Shri Anil Ravipudi at a press conference on his film
Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu
during the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. The 164-minute Telugu-language feature is among the five films selected for the Mainstream Cinema section of Indian Panorama at IFFI 2026. The director was joined by producers Shri Sahu Garapati and Ms. K. Sushmita and actor Ms. Catherine Tresa.
“Comedy is always a serious business,” remarked Shri Ravipudi, explaining the challenges of writing humour while balancing family emotions and the expectations associated with a superstar like Chiranjeevi. He observed that it is difficult to predict which jokes will resonate with audiences. Crediting his writing team for its support, the director said his endeavour has been to craft stories that appeal to audiences across age groups.
Written and directed by Shri Ravipudi,
Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu
follows a national security officer whose devotion to his profession leaves him estranged from his wife and children. Six years later, he seeks to reconnect with them by taking up a position at their school. Blending humour and action with family emotions, the film explores the tension between professional duty and personal relationships, and the possibility of reconciliation.
Reflecting on his experience of directing Chiranjeevi, Shri Ravipudi recalled growing up watching the veteran actor’s films. His familiarity with the actor’s diverse roles over the years helped him develop a simple family narrative that showcased Chiranjeevi’s distinctive strengths.
Speaking about his association with the films being released around Sankranti, the director said the festive season naturally lends itself to family entertainers, as families come together and visit theatres. He observed that cinema offers audiences much-needed relief from the stresses of everyday life, adding that the joy of bringing smiles to their faces was a major motivation for him to continue making such films.
Ms. Catherine Tresa, who plays an important character in the film, described working alongside the veteran actor as a valuable learning experience. Speaking about her transition from serious roles to lighter ones, she emphasised the importance of versatility and understanding the director’s vision. She also expressed happiness at the film’s selection for IFFI, having wanted to connect with a wider audience through a commercial entertainer.
Welcoming the recognition of mainstream cinema at film festivals, Shri Ravipudi appreciated the jury’s efforts to accommodate different kinds of films. He observed that festivals could celebrate artistic and technical excellence while also recognising commercially successful films that connect with large audiences.
The film’s presentation at IFFI highlights the place of popular cinema alongside diverse cinematic traditions, celebrating stories that bring families together through humour, emotion and shared experiences.
The session was moderated by Swati Aggarwal.

title: ‘Bhai Band’ Brings a Melodious Tale of Brotherhood, Tradition and Changing Times to IFFI 2026
content:
Goa, 25 November 2026
Bhai Band
, a Gujarati film directed by Manish Saini, featured in the Gala Premier section of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 in Goa today. The film follows two brothers who run a traditional wedding band in their village. Their lives take an unexpected turn when a disagreement drives them apart. When one brother returns weeks later with a DJ system and massive speakers, armed with nothing more than a playlist on his phone, the traditional band faces an unexpected challenge. What follows is a story that examines the impact of technological advancement on traditional occupations and the relationships that hold families together.
Addressing a press conference organised by PIB today, Director Manish Saini emphasised that although rooted in the Gujarati language and cultural setting, the film's underlying message and plot are universal and relatable to audiences across India. He also highlighted the importance of popularising artistic expressions and stories rooted in regional cinema, enabling them to reach wider audiences. Saini said that he was particularly fond of the film’s title, as it can be interpreted both as a reference to the camaraderie between two brothers and as a reference to a wedding band.
Actor Prit Kamani described
Bhai Band
as a unique film, filled with colours and enthusiasm. Marking his first Gujarati film, he spoke about his experience of working with Director Manish Saini and appreciated the ease and creative freedom he experienced during the filmmaking process. The actor also shared an amusing anecdote from the casting process, recalling how he had himself requested the director to conduct a screen test before finalising him for the role.
Actor Chirag Katrecha spoke about the process of understanding and internalising his character to bring authenticity to the performance. He also highlighted the challenges involved in portraying a singer, describing it as a demanding yet engaging experience.
Sharing insights into her character, actress Shraddha Dangar described her character as a lovely and cheerful personality. Reflecting on her experience, she spoke warmly about the collaboration and the enjoyable time spent working with the entire team.
Through humour, music and an engaging narrative, Bhai Band brings to the screen a story that goes beyond the changing sound of wedding celebrations. It raises questions about the intersection of technology, traditional livelihoods and human relationships, while celebrating the cultural vibrancy of regional storytelling.

title: Baapya Explores Acceptance, Understanding and Relationships: Director Samir Tewari
subtitle: Art Mirrors Society and Guides Social Progress: Actor Girish Kulkarni
content:
Goa, 25 November 2026
Baapya
, a Marathi comedy-drama set in coastal Maharashtra, explores gender identity, family relationships and social acceptance through an intimate story of personal choices and changing societal perceptions. The film is featured in the Mainstream Cinema section of Indian Panorama at the 57th International Film Festival of India.
Baapya
Director cum Producer Samir Tewari and actor Girish Kulkarni interacted with the media at a press conference organised by PIB on the sidelines of the festival.
In his opening remarks, Samir Tewari emphasised that the film does not aim to preach or offer lessons to society, but simply tells a story about acceptance, understanding and relationships. "It's just a story about somebody wanting to become who they want to be, and people around them accepting them the way they are." he said.
Explaining his decision to make the film in Marathi, Tewari said he wanted to make an honest film rooted in a genuine script rather than one designed around an actor.
Recalling the challenges during production, Tewari said securing financial backing for the project was difficult, as potential investors considered its subject risky despite appreciating the script. Casting the lead character, Baapya, was another major challenge, as several actresses were hesitant about portraying a character whose gender identity differed from their own. He credited actress Rajashri Deshpande for taking up the role fearlessly and approaching it as a demanding creative challenge.
Reflecting on changing gender perceptions, Tewari said society is gradually moving towards blurring conventional distinctions between men and women. He observed that individual choices in clothing, behaviour and identity should not invite judgement or discrimination.
"
Within every man there is a woman and within every woman there is a man. The faster a society progresses, the more the lines will blur between gender," he remarked, emphasising the need to move beyond rigid social notions.
Actor Girish Kulkarni highlighted the importance of treating every individual with dignity and without prejudice. Drawing an analogy from nature, he said people accept the diversity of trees and plants without judging their forms, and the same spirit should guide human relationships.
Observing that art can play a significant role in shaping society, Kulkarni said cinema and other art forms serve not only as mirrors of contemporary realities but also as guides for social progress. He added that
Baapya
seeks to reinterpret traditions in the light of changing times without abandoning cultural roots.
"
We aren't forgetting our tradition; we are bringing it forward by interpreting it in a new way, and while strengthening our own roots, we are also thinking ahead. And then we have this immense love coming out of that process,” he pointed out.
Kulkarni further described acceptance and love as the film's underlying spirit, saying that embracing differences in language, clothing and identity reflects India's distinctive strength of unity in diversity. Referring to India's philosophical traditions, he said acceptance and the ability to look at the present without prejudice are deeply rooted in Indian thought. "I feel like I personally experienced that journey within myself, and that's how we were able to translate it onto celluloid," he said.
Highlighting the significance of IFFI as a platform for cultural and intellectual exchange, Kulkarni said the festival brings together filmmakers and audiences from India and abroad, creating opportunities to encounter diverse cinematic perspectives and engage in meaningful discussions.
The Press Conferenece was moderated by Supriya Ghaytadak.

title: Sixth Edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow Celebrates Emerging Filmmaking Talent at IFFI 2026
subtitle:
100 young creators from 13 filmmaking disciplines complete an intensive 48-hour filmmaking challenge

Stay connected and continue working as a team; CMOT is just the beginning: IFFI Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker
content:
Goa, 25 November 2026
From developing a story to bringing it to the screen, 100 young creative professionals put their filmmaking skills to the test in an intensive 48-hour challenge as the sixth edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow (CMOT) concluded at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today. The initiative brought together emerging talent from across the country, culminating in the screening of films created by five teams and the presentation of awards across fifteen categories.
The concluding ceremony was attended by Festival Director of the 57
th
IFFI and filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker; Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Prabhat; Managing Director of NFDC and Vice-Chancellor of FTII, Dhiraj Singh and members of jury. The Great Grand Jury was comprised of Aimee Baruah, Premraj, Madhu Apsara, Rumi Jaffrey, and Medha Kherdekar Reddy.
Winners of CMOT 2026
1. Best Film: One Last Stop, directed by Mohak Gandhi (Red Team), awarded ₹5 lakh.
2. Runner-up Film: A Little Something, directed by Tamanna Thakur (Green Team), awarded ₹3 lakh.
3. Best Director: Tamanna Thakur, A Little Something (Green Team).
4. Best Actor: Siddhi Parkar, Shells (Blue Team).
5. Best Cinematographer: Triasha Manna, One Last Stop (Red Team).
6. Best Editor: Nayan Chotaliya and Manav Agarwal, A Little Something (Green Team).
7. Best Scriptwriter: Jithin S, Shells (Blue Team).
8. Best Sound Design: Aswin Ashok, Two Sunsets and Zero Sunrises (Yellow Team).
9. Best Playback Singer: Sree Parvati S, Shells (Blue Team).
10. Best Music Composer: Akshay Anmol Katore, Neel Machli (Beige Team).
11. Best Costume Design: Srushti Wagh and Rupalika Paul, One Last Stop (Red Team).
12. Best Hair and Makeup Artist: Kashish Jaiswal, Shells (Blue Team).
13. Best Art Design: Srushti Wagh and Rupalika Paul, One Last Stop (Red Team).
14. Best Animation and VFX Artist: Harsh Sahani and Prakash Kumar Mehta, Neel Machli (Beige Team).
15. Best Voice-over/Dubbing: Sudeksha Sarkar, A Little Something (Green Team).
A bridge to the industry
Congratulating the participants on completing the 48-hour filmmaking challenge, Additional Secretary Prabhat described CMOT as a bridge between emerging talent and the film industry. He said the initiative provides young creators with an opportunity to demonstrate their abilities and connect with industry professionals.
Referring to this year’s theme, ‘
Roots & Wings: Honouring our Roots, Embracing our Futur
e,’
he highlighted the coming together of cultural heritage, innovation and technology. He also pointed to the growing opportunities in the AVGC-XR sector, which is opening new avenues for young professionals
in the creative industries.
Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker congratulated all the teams on their work and emphasised that filmmaking is inherently collaborative. He reminded the participants that a film is never the work of one individual, but the outcome of several creative disciplines coming together. Encouraging them to maintain the bonds formed during the challenge, he urged the young filmmakers to stay connected, continue working as teams and build on the experience, describing CMOT as just the beginning of their journey.
48 hours, five teams, one creative challenge
The filmmaking challenge began on 21 November, with the 100 participants divided into five teams of 20, identified by the colours Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, and Beige. Working under the common theme ‘Roots & Wings: Honouring our Roots, Embracing our Future,’ each team was tasked with conceptualising, shooting and completing a short film within 48 hours.
The challenge brought together participants from 13 filmmaking disciplines, including direction, acting, cinematography, editing, sound design, scriptwriting, art direction, animation, visual effects, music composition, playback singing, hair and makeup, and costume design. After shooting at locations across Goa, the teams moved to the dedicated post-production hub at Kala Academy, where they worked against the clock on editing, sound mixing and visual finishing to meet the deadline.
The resulting films reflected the participants’ creative interpretations of the theme, as well as their ability to collaborate across disciplines and deliver under demanding conditions.
Building pathways for emerging talent
Since its inception in 2021, CMOT has evolved into a platform connecting emerging creative professionals with the media and entertainment industry. Its alumni have gone on to work on international productions and received recognition at platforms and festivals including Cannes, the Berlinale, the Toronto International Film Festival and the International Emmy Awards.
In a notable outcome from the previous edition, 18 participants were selected by Mukesh Chhabra Casting Company (MCCC), demonstrating the initiative’s potential to translate emerging talent into professional opportunities.
The Film and Television Institute of India (FTII) curated and conducted the filmmaking challenge in collaboration with the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC). FTII faculty members mentored the participants throughout the process, while the Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG) facilitated shooting permissions at locations across the state.

title: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Signs MoU with Directorate General of Training to Skill 1 Lakh Youth under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
subtitle:
Ministry of Jal Shakti partners with Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship to strengthen the skilled workforce for sustainable rural water supply services

Initiative to Create New Employment Opportunities for Rural Youth by Building a Skilled Local Workforce of ‘Nal Jal Mitras’

Programme to Roll Out Water Supply Operation and Maintenance Training Through ITIs and NSTIs Nationwide
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant stride towards ensuring long-term sustainability of rural drinking water infrastructure and generating local employment, the
Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS)
, Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS), and the
Directorate General of Training (DGT)
, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), today signed a
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)
for the
Water Supply Operation & Maintenance Skilling Programme (Nal Jal Mitra)
under the
Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 (JJM 2.0)
.
The MoU was signed in the presence of Shri C. R. Patil, Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri V. Somanna, Hon’ble Minister of State, Jal Shakti and Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, at the residence office of Hon’ble MoJS, New Delhi.
The agreement was formally executed by
Smt. Swati Meena Naik, Joint Secretary, NJJM
and
Shri Sunil Kumar Gupta
,
Deputy Director General, DGT.
Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MoSDE, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, NJJM, and senior officials from both Ministries were present during the MoU signing.
The Hon’ble Union Ministers present on the occasion appreciated the initiative, highlighting its significance in strengthening rural water supply systems through a skilled local workforce and creating livelihood opportunities for rural youth. They acknowledged the importance of inter-ministerial collaboration under the ‘whole of government’ approach in leveraging the country’s vocational training infrastructure to support the objectives of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
Briefing on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and the skilling initiative,
Shri Ashok K.K. Meena
, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, said that with nearly 16 crore rural households now connected through tap water supply systems, the next priority is establishing a robust operation and maintenance ecosystem capable of supporting these assets over the long term. He stressed that timely technical support should be available within villages and nearby areas so that routine operational issues can be addressed quickly without dependence on external agencies.
Shri Meena highlighted that the partnership between DDWS and DGT would connect India's vocational training ecosystem directly with the rural water sector. Through structured classroom learning and hands-on exposure at functioning village water supply schemes, a new cadre of trained youth will be developed to support operations and maintenance activities. He added that the database of certified candidates would be made available at district and Gram Panchayat levels, enabling States and UTs to engage skilled personnel in accordance with their respective policies and requirements.
The MoU formalises a collaborative framework between DDWS and DGT for implementing the Water Supply Operation & Maintenance Skilling Programme under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. The initiative aims to create a trained and certified workforce capable of supporting the operation and maintenance of rural piped water supply systems while leveraging the existing ITI and NSTI network across the country.
Key Features of the Programme
Scale & Financial Outlay:
The MoU targets the training and certification of
at least 1,00,000 (one lakh) candidates
during the extended period of the Jal Jeevan Mission, with an estimated outlay of approximately
₹111.93 crore
borne entirely by DDWS from its departmental-level expenditure.
165-Hour NSQF-Aligned Course:
Developed by the
Central Staff Training and Research Institute (CSTARI)
under DGT in consultation with DDWS and approved by
NCVET
, the short-term training (STT) course comprises
120 hours of institutional training
(theory and practical) and
45 hours of mandatory On-the-Job Training (OJT)
.
Target Group & Dual Certification:
Offered as an optional elective for
existing and pass-out trainees of Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) Fitter and Plumber trades
across Government ITIs and NSTIs. On successful completion, trainees will receive an NSQF-aligned
Short-Term Training (STT) certificate
from DGT in addition to their
National Trade Certificate (NTC)
.
Hands-on Competencies & Field Exposure:
The curriculum covers plumbing, water distribution systems, pumps and motors, basic electrical work, water quality monitoring, and routine O&M. Through the 45-hour OJT—facilitated by DDWS at functioning rural piped water supply schemes—trainees will gain direct experience in real-world village conditions.
Implementation & Governance:
The
National Instructional Media Institute (NIMI)
, a subordinate office of DGT, will serve as the
Training Partner
for fund disbursement, training coordination, assessment, and certification. DDWS will support trainer orientation, OJT site identification, and share the database of certified candidates at District and Gram Panchayat levels for potential engagement in O&M roles in accordance with respective State HR policies. A
Joint Steering Committee
, chaired by an officer not below the rank of Joint Secretary, DDWS, will oversee rollout, targets, and fund utilisation.
The partnership between DDWS and DGT marks a significant step towards institutionalising operation and maintenance capacity within India's rural water sector. By embedding water supply O&M skilling within the country's established vocational training ecosystem, the initiative will create a sustainable pipeline of certified Nal Jal Mitras equipped with technical and field-level competencies. The programme is expected to support long-term functionality of rural piped water supply infrastructure, strengthen service delivery at the grassroots, and generate meaningful livelihood opportunities for rural youth, thereby contributing to the objectives of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.

title: India's MSME Growth Story Hits a New High: 10 Crore Registrations, 10 Crore Steps for a Vibrant and Strong Aatmanirbhar Bharat!
subtitle: Transforming MSME Registration; from paper work to a seamless digital ecosystem
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India's Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector has achieved a milestone, crossing
10 crore registrations on the Udyam Registration Portal and Udyam Assist Platform on 30 October 2026
. This achievement marks a defining moment in India's journey towards building a more formalised, inclusive and digitally empowered MSME sector.
A Landmark Achievement in MSME Formalisation.
The combined strength of the Udyam Registration Portal and Udyam Assist Platform has taken India's MSME formalisation journey to a new level. The growth from
1.02 crore registrations in 2020 to over 10 crore in 2026
demonstrates the increasing adoption of digital platforms and the Government's sustained commitment to bringing enterprises into the formal economic framework.
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises launched the Udyam Registration Portal on 1 July 2020
,
providing enterprises with a simple, transparent, online and paperless platform for registration. This digital initiative has significantly streamlined registration procedures, enhanced ease of doing business and enabled enterprises to become part of India's formal economic ecosystem.
Evolution of MSME Registration in India: From EM-II to Udyam Registration
India's MSME registration framework has evolved significantly over the years, moving from a largely physical and document-intensive process to a technology-driven, entrepreneur-friendly digital ecosystem.
Key milestones in this journey:
1. Entrepreneurs Memorandum (EM-II) – 2006 to 17 September 2015
MSME registration was primarily a physical process, requiring entrepreneurs to submit applications along with the requisite documents for verification by the District Industries Centre (DIC). During this nine-year period,
21.96 lakh MSMEs
were registered.
2. Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) – 18 September 2015 to 30 June 2020
A significant shift towards digital registration took place with the introduction of the Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM). Based on Aadhaar, the online system simplified the earlier registration procedure and reduced the compliance burden on entrepreneurs. Around 1.02 crore MSMEs
registered during this five-year period.
3. Udyam Registration – From 1 July 2020
A major digital transformation was ushered in with the launch of the Udyam Registration Portal. The registration process became fully online, paperless and based on self-declaration, eliminating the requirement for physical documents or proof uploads.
Integration with Aadhaar and PAN-based details, along with GST and Income Tax databases, further streamlined the registration process. The system also eliminated the requirement for renewal and made registration completely free of cost, making formalisation simpler and more accessible for entrepreneurs across the country.
4. Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) – From 11 January 2023
Recognising that a large number of micro-enterprises, particularly those operating in the informal sector, faced difficulties in accessing registration facilities, the Ministry introduced the Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) on 11 January 2023.
The platform facilitates the formalisation of eligible informal micro-enterprises through a simplified mechanism involving designated financial institutions and other partner agencies.
Udyam: Enabling Access, Recognition and Inclusive Growth
Udyam registration supports the identification of enterprises by banks and financial institutions, facilitating the implementation of initiatives such as the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), Priority Sector Lending and other credit and Finance related programmes.
It strengthens the foundation for inclusive economic development by bringing women entrepreneurs, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs, rural enterprises, traditional artisans and other disadvantaged sections into the formal economic framework.
Furthermore, formal recognition through Udyam supports the broader objectives of various Government initiatives, including the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), National SC-ST Hub, Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises and other entrepreneurship development programmes, subject to applicable eligibility requirements.
Driving Inclusive Growth: Participation of Women
The registration data of both Udyam and Udyam Assist reflects the following:
Women-led MSMEs:
3.76 crore registrations, accounting for
37.8%
.
These figures underline the role of digital registration in expanding formal recognition among diverse sections of society and strengthening the foundation of inclusive entrepreneurship.
The milestone of 10 crore registrations is not merely a number; it represents millions of enterprises taking steps towards formal recognition and becoming part of India's growth story. It reflects the growing confidence of entrepreneurs in India's digital ecosystem and the collective momentum towards a stronger, more inclusive and self-reliant economy.

The Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR), Government of India, will organize the first Regional Workshop on implementation of the Sixteenth Finance Commission (XVI FC) Recommendations for Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) grants in Goa tomorrow, 26 November 2026. Smt. Mukta Shekhar, Joint Secretary, MoPR, will be joined by senior officers from the participating States of Goa, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan. The Workshop seeks to build a shared understanding of the 16th Finance Commission’s recommendations, the Operational Guidelines and the compliance conditions among the Western Region States, so that the 16th Finance Commission grants reach Panchayats on time and translate into visible improvements in the lives of rural citizens.
The Sixteenth Finance Commission has recommended grants of ₹4,35,236 crore to PRIs (Panchayati Raj Institutions) / RLBs (Rural Local Bodies) across all 28 States for the award period 2026-27 to 2030-31. The Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, issued the Operational Guidelines for their implementation on 21 May 2026. The Commission has also recommended that MoPR extend guidance and handholding support to States and organise Regional Workshops to familiarise them with various aspects of the recommendations. The Goa Workshop is the first in this series.
The Workshop builds on the National Workshop of State Panchayati Raj Ministers held by MoPR on 3 July 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, to discuss implementation of the 16th FC recommendations for PRIs/ RLBs. While the National Workshop set the policy direction, the Regional Workshops carry the dialogue closer to the officers responsible for delivery on the ground.
Reflecting the Ministry’s continuing efforts and focus on augmentation of Own Sources of Revenue (OSR), the Workshop also seeks to deliberate on experiences and best practices that enhance the fiscal self-reliance of Panchayats. Elected Representatives and officers from the host State, Goa, are also expected to participate.
Financially empowered, capable and accountable Panchayats are central to the vision of Atmanirbhar Panchayat and Viksit Panchayat, which pave the way for Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat. Timely devolution of Finance Commission grants, together with steadily growing OSR, will enable Panchayats to plan, deliver and serve their communities with greater confidence. The Workshop is being hosted with the support of the Department of Panchayati Raj, Government of Goa, and the Ministry looks forward to a productive and collaborative exchange among all participating States.

title: NHAI to Ensure Availability of Incident Management Services Before Opening of National Highway Stretches
subtitle: New guidelines strengthen emergency response mechanism through availability of ambulances, patrol vehicles and tow-away cranes
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In order to strengthen emergency services on National Highways, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued guidelines to ensure availability of Incident Management Services (IMS) on National Highways before opening of stretch to traffic. The objective is to strengthen road safety and ensure timely assistance to National Highway users during accidents, vehicle breakdowns and other emergencies.
Incident Management Services include availability of ambulances, route patrolling vehicles and tow-away cranes on National Highways. These services are supported by the integration of on-location teams with NHAI’s 1033 National Highway Helpline and coordination with local police, fire services and hospitals.
Ensuring IMS availability across National Highway network
The guidelines prescribe arrangements for ensuring availability of these services on different categories of National Highway stretches. On operational National Highway stretches, ambulances are positioned at the user fee plazas or other suitable locations, based on accident data and requirement of the stretch.
For National Highways entrusted to NHAI by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, ambulances will be deployed through a centralised agency in accordance with the delegated powers of NHAI field offices. Route patrolling vehicles and tow-away cranes will be arranged through separate tenders or as part of highway maintenance and strengthening works.
Apart from this, on National Highway stretches that have not been entrusted to NHAI but are tolled by NHAI, deployment of IMS will follow the procedure laid down by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. Under this, ambulances will be deployed through NHAI’s centralised agency in coordination with the concerned Regional Office of the Ministry/NHIDCL, while route patrolling vehicles and tow-away cranes on such stretches will be arranged by the concerned authority.
With this initiative, NHAI aims to provide National Highway users with timely assistance and enhance overall safety on the National Highway network across the country.

content:
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister for Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, and Smt. Annapurna Devi, Union Minister for Women and Child Development, today launched the fifth edition of “Nayi Chetna: Pahal Badlaav Ki”, the National Campaign on Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment, at NASC Complex, PUSA, New Delhi. Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development; Shri Anil Malik, Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development; and Shri Niraj Verma, Secretary, Department of Justice, were present, along with senior officials of participating Ministries, State Governments, development partners and women leaders from across the country.
The centrepiece of the event was a landmark Quadripartite MoU on the Violence-Free Village Initiative (VFVI), signed by the Department of Rural Development, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Department of Justice and the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The MoU links DAY-NRLM’s Gender Resource Centres with One Stop Centres, Women Helpline 181, Disha 2.0 and legal aid services into a single chain of support, from prevention and protection to legal assistance and rehabilitation. To be piloted in 9 States and Union Territories, it rests on a simple promise: no woman facing violence should be left to find her way to help alone.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan affirmed that women’s empowerment, dignity and respect lie at the heart of the vision of Viksit Bharat, and lauded the contribution of nearly 3.75 crore Lakhpati Didis to the rural economy. Asserting that economic independence must go hand in hand with dignity, safety and equal opportunity, he called for collective effort to challenge patriarchal mindsets. Describing the MoU as a framework that brings safety, justice, rehabilitation and livelihood support together, he urged States, SHGs, Anganwadi networks and communities to turn the campaign into sustained grassroots action and to integrate the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan towards drug-free and violence-free villages.
Smt. Annapurna Devi highlighted the role of community institutions in taking the campaign to every household. Calling for wider use of support services, she urged citizens to remember, save and share Women Helpline 181 and Emergency Response Number 112, so that no woman in distress goes without timely help.
Shri Rohit Kansal traced Nayi Chetna’s journey from an awareness campaign to a nationwide, community-led movement, with 5.3 crore participants and nearly 7,000 Gender Resource Centres established so far. The fifth edition, he said, will turn that awareness and community trust into effective support, legal assistance and timely access to justice.
Shri Anil Malik called for seamless convergence of helplines, legal services and support institutions, backed by timely response and consistent follow-up. Highlighting the 16-day action agenda, he underlined the collective responsibility of families, communities and institutions towards women’s safety.
Shri Niraj Verma stressed the need to turn existing legal safeguards into services women can actually reach, particularly in rural and remote areas. He highlighted the role of NALSA, Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu, paralegal volunteers and Gender Resource Centres in strengthening legal awareness, referrals and free legal aid.
An Inter-Ministerial Joint Advisory was also unveiled, extending the Whole-of-Government approach to address gender-based discrimination and violence and advance women’s economic empowerment. The collaborating Ministries/Departments are: Rural Development, Women and Child Development; School Education and Literacy; Home Affairs; Panchayati Raj; Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Social Justice and Empowerment; Youth Affairs and Sports; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises; Information and Broadcasting; Justice; Labour and Employment; Revenue; and Road Transport and Highways.
Led by DAY-NRLM, the campaign will run across all States and Union Territories until 23 December 2026, built around four themes: Identity, Assetization, Mobility, and Redistribution of Unpaid Care Work. Through Self-Help Groups and community institutions, it will reach rural India with awareness drives, rallies, community meetings, street plays and dialogues with men and youth.
The event also saw the release of the Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report and the Nayi Chetna Anthem, and Gender Champions and One Stop Centre administrators shared experiences from the field. SHG women, Anganwadi workers, State Rural Livelihoods Missions and civil society partners took part in large numbers, reaffirming Nayi Chetna as a true Jan Andolan for gender equality.

content:
The Department of Rural Development (DoRD) and the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) today signed an Agreement for Management and Technical Support for the Interest Subvention Scheme for women Self Help Groups and the Women Enterprise Acceleration Fund (WEAF) under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). The Agreement was signed by Shri Vipin Kumar, Additional Secretary, DoRD, and Shri Ajay Kumar Sood, Deputy Managing Director, NABARD in the presence of Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Rural Development; Dr. Shaji Krishnan V, Chairman, NABARD. Following the signing, the Secretary and the Chairman jointly launched the Interest Subvention Portal.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Rural Development, said that the SHG movement, having achieved remarkable outreach and scale, is now entering a new phase focused on enterprise development. Over Rs. 14 lakh crore has already been mobilised as formal credit for SHGs, steadily replacing informal sources of credit in rural areas. Over the next five years, the Department aims to facilitate an additional Rs. 10 lakh crore for SHGs and Rs. 1 lakh crore for individual enterprises.
“Interest subvention will make credit more affordable, reimbursement of guarantee fees will make collateral-free credit safer, and the new portal will make the process faster,”
the Secretary said. He called upon DoRD and NABARD to work closely to design customised credit products for SHG members, strengthen enterprise support systems, bridge information gaps on schemes, and build capacities for a robust and sustainable SHG ecosystem.
Under the Agreement, NABARD will serve as the single nodal agency for both schemes, covering Public Sector, Private Sector, Small Finance, Regional Rural and Cooperative Banks, and will provide technical, managerial and implementation support to the Department. Banks will now work with one set of rules, one reconciliation process and one point of accountability.
“This partnership combines NABARD’s institutional strengths with DAY-NRLM’s community network to accelerate the transition of SHG women from livelihoods to viable enterprises,”
said Dr. Shaji Krishnan V, Chairman, NABARD. He reaffirmed NABARD’s commitment to deepening its collaboration with the Department to advance financial inclusion and women-led development.
Shri Vipin Kumar, Additional Secretary, Rural Development, said that women SHGs have earned a trusted place in the formal banking system through their financial discipline and creditworthiness.
“The question before us is no longer whether banks should lend to rural women, but how quickly, how cheaply and how far that credit can take them,”
he remarked. He added that with every participating bank onboarded on the portal, claims would be processed and settled on time.
The Agreement will strengthen the way credit support reaches rural women. Predictable and prompt reimbursement will give banks greater confidence to extend larger loans to women’s collectives, while lower costs and shared risk will open the door to enterprise finance for women.  Over time, the portal’s real-time data will offer a clear view of how credit flows to rural women, enabling sharper targeting and better-informed policy under DAY-NRLM. Together, these measures mark a decisive step in turning Lakhpati Didis into rural entrepreneurs and employers.

content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh today highlighted India’s expanding StartUp ecosystem, growing capabilities in biotechnology and healthcare innovation, and the increasing role of artificial intelligence (AI), genomics and precision medicine in transforming healthcare, while addressing HealthX Elevate 2026.
The Minister noted that India has emerged as the world’s third-largest start-up ecosystem, with more than 60 per cent of StartUps coming from Tier-II and Tier-III cities and smaller towns.
The event, themed around healthcare start-ups and innovation, brought together healthcare leaders, entrepreneurs, investors and experts to discuss the evolving landscape of healthcare innovation in India.
Speaking during a Fire Chat session, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India’s start-up ecosystem has undergone a remarkable transformation, expanding from around 350 start-ups in 2014 to more than 2.5 lakh today. He noted that India has emerged as the world’s third-largest start-up ecosystem, with more than 60 per cent of start-ups coming from Tier-II and Tier-III cities.
The Minister said that the growth of start-ups is no longer confined to major metropolitan hubs such as Bengaluru, Delhi and Mumbai. Digital access and an enabling ecosystem have made information, resources and opportunities available to aspiring entrepreneurs across the country, allowing talent from smaller cities and towns to participate in the start-up movement.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the emergence of entrepreneurship beyond conventional technology and science-led fields. Referring to the growth of agri-based start-ups, he said that entrepreneurial success does not necessarily require a highly advanced academic qualification, but calls for passion, focus and the ability to use technology effectively. He added that the Government is extending technological and financial support to encourage entrepreneurship.
The Minister highlighted the significant expansion of India’s biotechnology start-up ecosystem, which, he said, has grown from around 50–60 start-ups in 2014 to nearly 10,000 today. He said that India is increasingly developing solutions not only for diseases prevalent in tropical regions, but also for conditions that were earlier primarily associated with other parts of the world.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India’s progress in vaccines has transformed the way the country’s healthcare capabilities are viewed globally. He referred to the development of the country’s DNA vaccine for COVID-19 and its supply to around 30 countries. He also highlighted advances in genetic and therapeutic research, including a successful trial of a genetic therapy for haemophilia, the findings of which were published in the New England Journal of Medicine.
Referring to developments in nuclear medicine, the Minister said that Indian researchers are working on cost-effective solutions for diseases, including acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. He noted that India is moving beyond addressing diseases traditionally associated with the country and is developing affordable therapeutic and diagnostic solutions with wider global relevance.
Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised the need for greater private-sector participation in biotechnology, healthcare research and innovation. He said that the Government is encouraging private partners to contribute to research and development, and expressed hope that India would produce a globally recognised blockbuster drug in the coming decade.
The Minister also highlighted India’s unique advantage in healthcare research due to its diverse population and genetic resources. He said that a comprehensive understanding of genetic data could help researchers generate insights relevant not only to India but also to the global scientific community.
On the role of artificial intelligence in healthcare, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that AI should be viewed as an enabling tool across disciplines rather than as a separate domain. He highlighted its potential in diagnosis, data collection and analysis, noting that processes which earlier took hours or days could now be completed in minutes with AI support.
Referring to the Genome India initiative, the Minister said that AI is facilitating the analysis of genetic information and supporting the study of diverse population groups. He noted that the Government had completed gene sequencing of 10,000 individuals, with the data covering 80 different population groups.
The Minister said that India is entering an era of individualised and precision medicine, in which treatment may be tailored to the genetic profile, lifestyle, environment and molecular characteristics of each patient. He noted that advances in research could enable doctors to move towards more personalised prescriptions, even for patients presenting with similar disease or investigation profiles.
He also underscored the growing importance of preventive healthcare, early detection and research into biomarkers that may help identify the likelihood of diseases before they develop. Referring to research on diabetes-related pregnancy, he said that scientists are working on biomarkers that could help assess the risk of diabetes in women at the time of delivery, enabling more targeted follow-up and preventive care.
During the interaction, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India is witnessing a gradual shift towards deep-tech and science-led enterprises, including biotechnology, quantum technology, artificial intelligence and space. He noted that the opening of new sectors to private participation is creating opportunities for entrepreneurs and said that the emergence of successful businesses in these areas would encourage further industry investment.
Responding to a question on the challenges faced by deep-tech start-ups in securing their first major customer, the Minister said that the Government is working towards creating a more enabling environment. He referred to changes made to allow greater risk-taking in the support extended to start-ups, including the removal of a requirement under a CSIR provision that a start-up must have been in existence for at least three years before it could receive funding.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the importance of collaboration between government, industry, researchers and healthcare professionals. He said that the era of working in silos is over and that pooling expertise, resources and investment can help accelerate innovation and bring research closer to practical application.
Concluding his remarks, the Minister emphasised that the goal of healthcare innovation must be to ensure affordable and accessible healthcare for all. He said that this would require an integrated, whole-of-nation approach, with the government, industry and medical professionals working together, alongside a stronger culture of philanthropy to support research and innovation.

title: First North-East India-Specific antivenom developed against neglected Pit Vipers species
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A novel antivenom specifically effective against the venom of two particular pit vipers common in the North Eastern states can help improve treatment for snake bites common in these areas.   and Meghalaya states in order to close this gap in snakebite treatment.
Northeast India is home to a wide variety of venomous snakes, making snakebite a major public health concern. However, India's "Big Four" snakes—Russell's viper, spectacled cobra, common krait, and saw-scaled viper—are the main targets of commercially marketed antivenom. The effectiveness of this polyvalent antivenom against a number of medically significant venomous snakes in Northeast India has been shown to be limited.
Snake bites from pit vipers—the Pope's pit viper (
Trimeresurus popeiorum
) and the red-tailed bamboo pit viper (
Trimeresurus erythrurus
) found in the North Eastern states are a common medical emergency in these areas. Snakebite is regarded as a neglected tropical disease and a medical emergency by the World Health Organization (WHO). The absence of antivenoms that can effective against venoms of these specific snakes leads to the the antivenom crisis in Northeast India, according to a recent study.
Fig:
A schematic diagram depicting the superior neutralizing activity of Bi-AV compared to Indian PAV against pit vipers from North-east India.
A research team led by Prof. Ashis K. Mukherjee, Director of the Institute of Advanced Study in Science and Technology (IASST), Guwahati, an Autonomous Institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) has created a novel equine F(ab)2 bivalent antivenom that is specifically effective against the venom of
T. erythrurus
and
T. popeiorum
that were collected from Mizoram and Meghalaya states in order to close this gap in snakebite treatment.
Researchers from IASST, Guwahati, Premium Serums and Vaccines Pvt. Ltd., Pune, Amrita Research Center Delhi-NCR, Mizoram University, and Aaranyak, Guwahati, collaborated on the project to demonstrate academic-industry cooperation.
In laboratory and preclinical investigations, the novel bivalent antivenom showed noticeably superior protection against pit viper envenomation of the NE region as compared to Indian polyvalent antivenom (Figure 1). Pit viper envenomation is characterized by disruptions in blood coagulation and injury to local and organ tissue, both of which are significantly reduced by the novel antivenom.
Prof. Mukherjee, who led the research stated that additional clinical and regulatory testing will be necessary before this novel antivenom is routinely used on patients and he is hopeful about it. The study published in the International Journal of Biological Macromolecules emphasizes the significance of creating region-specific antivenoms based on the snakes that cause severe envenomation in various regions of India, especially in Northeast India, where a number of medically significant species do not fit into the conventional "Big Four" paradigm.

title: India’s Bio-Economy Set to Reach 300 million Dollars by 2030; Dr. Jitendra Singh Urges Industry to Seize Opportunities in Next Biotechnology Revolution
subtitle:

Genomics and Multi-Omics Emerging as Strategic Technologies for Healthcare, Agriculture and Economic Growth: Dr. Jitendra Singh at CII Global Genomics Summit 2026

India’s Genetic Diversity Offers a Unique Global Advantage for Research and Innovation, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

Industry Participation, Private Investment and R&D Partnerships Crucial to Translating Scientific Discoveries into Economic Opportunities, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 3:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s bio-economy is set to reach 300 billion Dollars by 2030, with biotechnology set to drive the next Industrial Revolution, while Biotech Startups in India had already grown from just 50-60 in 2014 to over 11,000 today, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh said today, urging industry leaders, Startups and investors to seize emerging opportunities through greater investment and participation in genomics, multi-omics and advanced biotechnology.
Drawing a parallel with the transformative role of Information Technology in the previous industrial revolution, the Minister said that biotechnology is now emerging as a strategic technology platform that will shape the future of healthcare, agriculture and global economic competitiveness. He cautioned that businesses must adapt to the rapidly changing technological landscape, as those failing to embrace emerging technologies risk becoming irrelevant.
Addressing the CII Global Genomics Summit 2026, themed ‘Powering the Next Bioeconomy Through Genomics and Multi-omics’, at New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the summit provided an important platform to bring together the frontiers of science and technology with industry participation, translating scientific discoveries into healthcare solutions, economic opportunities and overall national development. He appreciated CII for bringing together industry representatives, startups and other stakeholders to advance India's biotechnology ecosystem.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the convergence of DNA sequencing, computational biology, Artificial Intelligence and different omics technologies, including metabolomics, transcriptomics and proteomics, would transform the understanding of complex diseases and enable more personalised healthcare. The same disease could require different treatment approaches for different individuals, making genomics an increasingly essential component of future medical practice. He said these technologies were no longer confined to research laboratories but were becoming indispensable for healthcare systems, businesses and nations seeking to remain competitive.
Emphasising India's unique advantage in genomic research, the Minister said the country's extraordinary genetic diversity could become a major global asset for research and development. India's diverse population groups and wide spectrum of diseases provide an extensive knowledge base for generating genomic data and developing solutions relevant to populations across the world. He said greater investment in genomic research would not only strengthen India's scientific capabilities but also create significant industrial and commercial opportunities.
Referring to the Genome India Project, he said whole-genome sequencing of 10,000 individuals representing 80 different population groups had already been undertaken, creating a valuable foundation for future research. He encouraged industry stakeholders to partner with government initiatives and translate this scientific resource into practical applications.
The Minister also drew attention to the extensive opportunities biotechnology offers in agriculture and livestock, beyond healthcare. Genomics and advanced biotechnology can help improve crop productivity, nutritional quality and resistance to pests and diseases, while supporting climate-resilient agriculture. In livestock, genomic applications can improve breeding practices and strengthen disease surveillance. He said the breadth of these applications offered businesses opportunities to specialise in different sectors and build sustainable, innovation-driven enterprises.
Speaking about India's rapidly expanding biotechnology ecosystem, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the government had introduced the BioE3 Policy- Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment, to accelerate biotechnology-led growth. The establishment of bio-foundries and other enabling infrastructure is aimed at supporting research, startups and industry in translating scientific discoveries into commercially viable products.
He said India's biotechnology startup ecosystem had grown from just 50-60 startups in 2014 to over 11,000 today, while the country's bio-economy had expanded from approximately 10 billion Dollars to nearly 195 billion Dollars. With the target of reaching 300 billion Dollars by 2030, India is entering a significant phase of biotechnology-led economic growth.
Citing India's growing global credibility in biotechnology, the Minister referred to the country's DNA vaccine for COVID-19, which was supplied to 30 countries, and said Indian biotechnology products were increasingly gaining international acceptance. He also referred to developments in HPV vaccines, research on haemophilia treatment and cost-effective CAR-T cell therapy for cancer at Tata Memorial Centre as examples of India's growing capabilities in advanced healthcare research. He said these achievements demonstrated that India had reached a stage where its biotechnology innovations could find wider global markets and attract greater industry participation.
Dr. Jitendra Singh called upon the private sector to increase investment in research and development and build stronger partnerships with government institutions, research organisations and startups. He referred to the ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme as an important initiative to accelerate private-sector participation in high-impact technologies. He also urged business leaders to support scientific research through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funding, particularly in areas such as cancer, diabetes and other major healthcare challenges. Describing research funding as a contribution to the well-being of society, he said investment in scientific research could create benefits extending far beyond individual businesses.
During his interaction with industry representatives, the Minister said that the biggest bottleneck in India's journey towards becoming a genomic powerhouse was the mindset, calling for greater openness towards emerging technologies and new business opportunities. Responding to concerns regarding regulatory processes for biotechnology products and advanced therapies, he said the government was working in consultation with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) to simplify procedures and address overlapping regulatory requirements. Concluding his address, Dr. Jitendra Singh called upon CII to act as an important bridge between the government and industry, facilitating greater investment, research partnerships and wider participation in India's biotechnology ecosystem. He said the success of India's scientific and technological progress would ultimately be measured not merely by the number of genomes sequenced or research papers published, but by the lives improved, products developed and economic opportunities created. title: Cabinet approves development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited under Public Private Partnership (PPP) Mode on Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) Basis
ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 3:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposed project for development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited (KPL) under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) basis, at an estimated project cost of Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST. The project envisages the development of a 900-metre-long container terminal with a design draft of 18 metres and an annual container-handling capacity of 2.0 million Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs), to be implemented in two phases.
Expenditure involved:
The estimated project cost of the PPP component is Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs.2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs.1,858.94 crore for Phase II. The investment is to be arranged by the selected concessionaire under the DBFOT model. The project proposal separately indicates an estimated dredging cost of Rs.450 crore to be borne by KPL.
Details:
(i)    The project envisages development of a 900-metre-long Second Container Terminal with a berth width of 30 metres and an annual container-handling capacity of 2.0 million TEUs. The terminal will be developed in two phases: Phase I with a capacity of 1.1 million TEUs and Phase II with a capacity of 0.9 million TEUs.
(ii)   The terminal is designed to handle large container vessels, including vessels of up to 24,346 TEUs and 400 metres in length overall, with a design draft of 18 metres. This will strengthen KPL’s ability to handle larger mainline vessels and improve connectivity with international shipping routes.
(iii)  The project is intended to meet the growing demand for containerised export-import (EXIM) cargo from the Chennai–Ennore industrial and economic region and the wider southern hinterland. Key cargo-generating sectors include automobiles and auto components, engineering goods, electronics, chemicals and other manufactured products.
(iv)  KPL handled 49.08 million tonnes of cargo and 1,008 vessels during FY 2025–26, including more than 7 lakh TEUs of container traffic. The existing container terminal has an installed capacity of 0.8 million TEUs per annum and handled approximately 0.7 million TEUs in FY 2025–26, representing utilisation of about 88%.
(v)   Container traffic in India has grown at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of about 7% over the last five years, while KPL’s container traffic has grown at approximately 9.9% during the same period. The feasibility study projects continued growth in container traffic in the south-eastern region, supporting the need to augment capacity at KPL.
(vi)  The project will be implemented on a DBFOT basis for a concession period of 40 years, including a construction period of 48 months. Phase I is scheduled for completion within 24 months from the Date of Award of Concession, with commercial operations commencing in the 25th month. Construction of Phase II will be undertaken from the 25th to the 48th month, with full commercial operations commencing in the 49th month.
(vii) The estimated project cost is Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs.2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs.1,858.94 crore for Phase II. The cost is to be financed by the selected concessionaire through the DBFOT framework. In addition, KPL is to incur an estimated Rs.450 crore towards dredging, as indicated in the project proposal.
(viii) The project is proposed to be implemented through a transparent, open global bidding process. The concessionaire will arrange the required financing and recover its investment through user charges in accordance with the provisions of the Concession Agreement and applicable tariff framework.
(ix)  The project is aligned with Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. It is expected to strengthen KPL’s position as a container gateway on India’s East Coast, improve the efficiency of the maritime logistics chain and support the growth of EXIM trade.
Implementation Strategy and Targets:
The project will be implemented by the selected concessionaire under the DBFOT model. Phase I, with a capacity of 1.1 million TEUs, is to be completed within 24 months from the Date of Award of Concession, and commercial operations are to commence in the 25th month. Phase II, with a capacity of 0.9 million TEUs, is to be completed by the 48th month, with full commercial operations commencing in the 49th month. The project proposal also provides for obtaining environmental and other necessary clearances in a time-bound manner before the bid due date.
Major Impact:
(i)  The additional capacity of 2.0 million TEUs per annum will strengthen KPL’s ability to accommodate growing container traffic and provide an additional gateway for EXIM cargo from the industrial clusters of Tamil Nadu and the adjoining hinterland.
(ii) The terminal’s design draft of 18 metres and capability to handle large container vessels are expected to improve international connectivity, facilitate direct calls by mainline vessels and reduce dependence on foreign deep-water hub ports and associated feedering costs.
(iii) The project is expected to improve maritime logistics efficiency, support trade and manufacturing, strengthen the port’s revenue potential and contribute to India’s maritime competitiveness.
(iv)     The project is expected to generate employment for approximately 750 persons directly and indirectly during construction and to increase about 800 persons during the operational phase.
(v) The project supports the objectives of Atmanirbhar Bharat by augmenting domestic port capacity and improving logistics support for industries and original equipment manufacturers in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and the adjoining hinterland.
(vi)     There will be no financial implication for the Government of India, as the investment in the PPP component will be arranged by the selected concessionaire.
Background:
(i)  Kamarajar Port Limited, formerly known as Ennore Port Limited, one of the 12 Major Ports of India and is wholly owned by Chennai Port Authority under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. Located on the east coast of Tamil Nadu near the Chennai industrial and economic region, the port handles a range of cargo, including coal, petroleum, oil and lubricants, LNG, LPG, containers, automobiles and general cargo.
(ii) During FY 2025–26, KPL recorded revenue of approximately Rs.1,280 crore and Profit Before Tax of Rs.924 crore. The port has recorded cargo growth at a CAGR of 13.64% over the last five years, reflecting the expansion of economic activity and trade in its hinterland.
(iii) The Chennai–Ennore region is a major industrial and manufacturing cluster of India. As trade and containerisation expand, additional container-handling capacity and efficient facilities for larger vessels are required to support the movement of EXIM cargo from Tamil Nadu, southern Andhra Pradesh and the wider southern hinterland.

title: MSDE partners with Ministry of Jal Shakti to skill one lakh youth under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
subtitle: The initiative will leverage the nationwide network of ITIs and NSTIs to develop a skilled workforce for rural water supply operations and maintenance
ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 8:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In an effort to align vocational training with emerging employment opportunities in the rural water sector, the Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti. The partnership will focus on implementing the Water Supply Operation & Maintenance Skilling Programme (Nal Jal Mitra) under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
The initiative aims to train and certify at least one lakh candidates, with an estimated financial outlay of ₹111.93 crore, entirely funded by DDWS.
The MoU was signed in the presence of Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti; and Shri V. Somanna, Minister of State, Jal Shakti.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, underscored that the initiative represents a significant example of inter-ministerial convergence aimed at addressing the skilled manpower requirements of a key national programme. He highlighted that the country's extensive network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) offers an effective platform for imparting specialised skills required for rural water supply operations and maintenance.
The 165-hour training programme has been developed by the Central Staff Training and Research Institute (CSTARI) under DGT, in consultation with DDWS. It will be offered as an optional elective to existing and former trainees of the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) Fitter and Plumber trades across ITIs and NSTIs.
The programme combines 120 hours of institutional training with 45 hours of mandatory on-the-job training. Candidates will learn plumbing, water distribution, pump and motor maintenance, basic electrical work and water quality monitoring. Upon successful completion, trainees will receive a National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF)-aligned short-term training certificate from DGT in addition to their National Trade Certificate (NTC).
The National Instructional Media Institute (NIMI), under DGT, will oversee training coordination, assessment, certification and fund disbursement. DDWS will make the details of certified candidates available at the district and Gram Panchayat levels, where they may be engaged for work as per the policies of the respective states.
Nearly 16 crore rural households in India now have tap water connections. Keeping these water supply systems functional requires trained personnel at the village level. The programme seeks to meet this requirement and, in the process, open up employment avenues for rural youth.

title: Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar, along with Shri B L Verma Launches ‘SAMAVESH’ and New e-Anudaan Portal to Strengthen Digital Governance and Inclusive Welfare Delivery
subtitle:
SAMAVESH Provides Unified Digital Access to Department’s Schemes, Services and Organisational Portals, Strengthening Citizen-Centric Governance

AI-Powered ‘Samajik Sahayak’ Chatbot to Facilitate Access to Welfare Scheme Information in 22 Indian Languages through BHASHINI

New e-Anudaan Portal to Simplify Grant-in-Aid Processes, Promote Ease of Doing Business and Strengthen Transparency and Accountability

date:

                25 NOV 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards strengthening technology-enabled governance and ensuring accessible, transparent and efficient delivery of social welfare services, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, along with Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, launched
SAMAVESH
(Single Access Mechanism for All Verticals of Empowerment & Social Harmony)
and the new
e-Anudaan Portal,
at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, in the National Capital here today.
The launch of SAMAVESH and the new e-Anudaan Portal marks a significant milestone in the Department’s digital transformation journey. These initiatives seek to make social welfare schemes and services more accessible, reduce procedural difficulties for beneficiaries and implementing organisations, and strengthen transparency, accountability and technology-enabled delivery of social welfare programmes.
Senior officers of the Ministry, representatives of NeGD, NIC, NGOs and other stakeholder organisations were also present on the occasion.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Virendra Kumar described the launching of SAMAVESH and new e-Anudaan portals as historical and a game changer and highlighted the Department’s commitment towards leveraging technology to strengthen the delivery of welfare schemes and services.
The Minister emphasised that SAMAVESH represents an important step towards integrated, transparent and citizen-centric governance by bringing the Department’s digital services onto a common platform.
Dr Kumar also underscored the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital integration and data-driven monitoring in improving the accessibility, transparency and effectiveness of welfare delivery.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri B. L. Verma highlighted the importance of making Government schemes more accessible to beneficiaries through simplified digital services. He emphasised that technology-driven initiatives such as SAMAVESH would enable citizens, particularly those belonging to disadvantaged and marginalised sections of society, to access information and services more conveniently while promoting transparency and inclusion.
Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, described the launch as a golden day in the Ministry’s history, marking a significant leap in digital governance with the integration of
33 different portals into a single SAMAVESH Portal.
He highlighted that
e-Anudaan 2.0 has reduced the number of forms from 283 to 182
, significantly easing procedural requirements for NGOs and institutions. The introduction of real-time remote inspections through Bharat VC with 15 minutes’ prior notice will further strengthen institutional monitoring and accountability. He also underscored the integration of AI, BHASHINI, DigiLocker and PFMS to enhance accessibility and efficiency.
Appreciating the efforts of the IT team under the leadership of Additional Secretary Ms. Mona K. Khandhar and Director Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, along with NeGD and NIC, the Secretary reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to advancing the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s vision of Ease of Living through technology-enabled governance.
Developed by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE), SAMAVESH provides a unified digital gateway to the Department’s schemes, services and organisational portals through
https://www.dosje.gov.in/samavesh-citizen-portals/
,enabling citizens to access a wide range of welfare-related information and services through a common platform.
The platform brings together six major scheme-related portals, including
Senior Citizens Welfare (SCW), National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), SAMBAL - National Helpline Against Atrocities (NHAA), Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) and Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE)
, covering welfare initiatives for transgender persons, rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging and Garima Greh.
SAMAVESH also brings together 12 organisational and institutional portals, including those of
Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF), Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation, National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC), National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK), Development and Welfare Board for De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities (DWBDNC)
and the Department’s Social Justice Portal.
The unified platform is designed to simplify access to welfare schemes and services, eliminating the need for citizens to search across multiple websites. A common login facility provides a more consistent user experience, while a consolidated Beneficiary Dashboard is intended to facilitate access to beneficiary-related information and strengthen monitoring of scheme implementation.
A key citizen-centric feature of SAMAVESH is
‘Samajik Sahayak’
,
an AI-powered chatbot that provides information on welfare schemes, eligibility criteria and services in 22 Indian languages through BHASHINI. The initiative seeks to overcome linguistic barriers and enable citizens to access Government information in languages they are comfortable with, thereby promoting digital inclusion and improving awareness of welfare schemes and services.
Integration with national digital platforms such as DigiLocker and the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) further supports secure access to documents and improved visibility of service and payment-related information. The platform also incorporates a common design and content framework aligned with applicable Government standards, including Guidelines for Indian Government Websites (GIGW) 3.0, Digital Brand Identity Manual (DBIM) and accessibility guidelines, with emphasis on secure, accessible and user-friendly digital services.
In a significant step towards strengthening multilingual digital service delivery, a
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)
was exchanged between Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, Director MoSJE & CEO, BHASHINI Shri Amitabh Nag,
on the occasion. The collaboration will facilitate the use of language technology to make information pertaining to the Department’s schemes and services accessible in multiple Indian languages. The initiative is expected to particularly benefit citizens facing linguistic barriers, enabling them to better understand scheme provisions and access welfare services more conveniently.
Shri Amresh Bahadur Pal, Director MoSJE, also exchanged an MoU with Shri Prashant Sinha, Chief Operating Officer, National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) to strengthen skill development and employment opportunities for beneficiaries under the Grant-in-Aid component of the
Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana
(PM-AJAY).
The partnership will facilitate access to skill development support and employment-oriented interventions, enabling beneficiaries to enhance their skills, improve employability and access better livelihood opportunities. The collaboration seeks to strengthen the link between welfare support, skill development and economic empowerment.
The newly launched
e-Anudaan Portal (
https://eanudaan.dosje.gov.in/
)
brings
grant-in-aid processes under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), SMILE, Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) and SHRESHTA (Modes 1 and 2)
onto a unified digital platform. The initiative seeks to promote Ease of Doing Business for Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), institutions and other implementing organisations through simplified application procedures, reduced documentation and automated document verification.
The portal provides a common Project ID, pre-filled information at different stages of application, application status dashboards and online notifications, thereby reducing repetitive data entry and enabling applicants to track their applications and pending actions more conveniently. Automated document checks and verification against relevant databases, including NGO Darpan and UDISE+, are intended to identify deficiencies at an early stage and minimise avoidable procedural delays.
The new e-Anudaan Portal also strengthens monitoring mechanisms through video-based e-Inspection, geo-tagged photographs and videos, and attendance records. Integration with PFMS enables tracking of fund disbursement and payments, thereby strengthening transparency and accountability in grant-in-aid management. These features are expected to improve the efficiency of grant administration for NGOs and institutions while supporting effective monitoring by the Department.
The development and implementation of SAMAVESH have been undertaken under the overall guidance and leadership of Ms. Mona K. Khandhar,  Additional Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Her guidance and continuous review have played an important role in facilitating coordination among the concerned Divisions and organisations and ensuring alignment of the initiative with the Department’s broader objectives of digital transformation and citizen-centric service delivery.
The IT Division of the Ministry has played a central coordinating role in the implementation of the initiative, working closely with concerned Divisions, organisations and technology partners, including the National e-Governance Division (NeGD) and the National Informatics Centre (NIC), for portal integration, migration, testing, content coordination, technical review and implementation of common digital standards.
The phased integration of scheme-related portals and organisational websites has facilitated the creation of a common digital gateway while supporting improved coordination and management of digital services across the Department.
Through these initiatives, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment reiterates its commitment towards building an inclusive, accessible and citizen-centric digital governance ecosystem, ensuring that the benefits of technology-driven welfare delivery reach disadvantaged and marginalised sections of society.

content:
Mr Raja’s
(name changed)
