Through the NAMASTE Scheme, efforts are being made to move sanitation work towards mechanisation, safety, formalisation and improved livelihood opportunities for workers.
For many workers engaged in sewer and septic tank cleaning, informal employment arrangements often mean uncertain income, hazardous working conditions and limited access to occupational safety or formal recognition.
For Raja, a 27-year-old graduate from Manipur, securing dignified and stable employment marked an important step towards greater financial security and professional recognition.
Despite completing his graduation, Raja had been working in informal sewer and septic tank cleaning under contractor-based arrangements. His work was characterised by irregular earnings, limited occupational safety measures and the absence of formal employment benefits. With his household dependent on uncertain income, the lack of employment stability posed continuing challenges.
The National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme seeks to formalise and improve the working conditions of Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs) by facilitating their identification, profiling and access to support and opportunities.
Through formal profiling under the NAMASTE Scheme, Raja was recognised as a Sewer and Septic Tank Worker, helping facilitate an opportunity for institutional employment.
On October 15, 2025, Raja was engaged as a Skilled Daily Wage Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) Operator at the High Court of Manipur. The employment opportunity provided him with a more predictable source of income and improved recognition of his work and skills.
He now earns ₹480 per day, amounting to approximately ₹14,400 per month. The transition from irregular contractor-based work to a formal institutional engagement has brought greater income predictability and improved employment conditions, helping him work towards long-term financial stability.
His experience reflects how formal recognition and employment opportunities can help sanitation workers move beyond informal arrangements towards greater stability, dignity and professional security.

title: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and Data Security Council of India (DSCI) sign MoU to enable trusted data sharing for official statistics
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 4:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and the Data Security Council of India (DSCI), set up by Nasscom, a not-for-profit industry body and think tank on data protection and cyber security, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi today. Dr Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, Shri Vinayak Godse, Chief Executive Officer, DSCI, and senior officers of the Ministry were present on the occasion. The MoU forms part of the Ministry’s efforts to strengthen the National Statistical System through collaboration with public and private sector institutions.
Statistical agencies now-a-days use data from both traditional and alternative sources, some of which contain personal identifiers. With Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 scheduled to come into force in 2027, data producing agencies need to gear up themselves by reviewing how they handle such data while maintaining privacy and confidentiality. This partnership will help develop protocols for sharing data in trusted manner within and across agencies while maintaining data quality, protecting privacy and preserving statistical confidentiality. As a first step, MoSPI and DSCI will jointly prepare a policy paper on trusted data flows and data management, drawing on international good practices in data protection and cybersecurity.
The collaboration will also cover joint research on data governance and technical support for the adoption of privacy-enhancing technologies and the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI). The MoU also provides facilitation for pilot projects with industry, academia, research institutions and international organisations and it will strengthen the national statistical ecosystem, by enabling responsible adoption of AI and emerging technologies.

title: Release of Report of the ‘Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts’ for the 2022-23 Series of National Accounts
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 2:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has undertaken the revision of the base year of National Accounts Statistics from 2011-12 to 2022-23. In this regard, the Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics (ACNAS), under the chairmanship of Prof. B. N. Goldar, had decided FY 2022-23 as the new base year. Five Sub-Committees were constituted under ACNAS to deliberate on specific subject areas relating to the compilation and presentation of National Accounts Statistics.
i. Sub-Committee for Incorporation of New Data Sources, Rates and Ratios
ii. Sub-Committee for Methodological Improvements
iii. Sub-Committee for Constant Price Estimates
iv. Sub Committee on Regional Accounts
v. Sub-Committee for SNA 2025 Update
The Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts, was constituted to review the concepts, definitions, classifications, data sources and estimation methodologies for the compilation of State Domestic Product (SDP) and District Domestic Product (DDP).
The Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts, under the chairmanship of
Prof. Ravindra H. Dholakia, Retired Professor, Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Ahmedabad
, undertook a comprehensive review of the existing methodologies for the compilation of State and District Domestic Product estimates in the context of the revised base year 2022–23. The deliberations involved experts from academia, the Reserve Bank of India, Central Ministries and Departments, State and Union Territory Directorates of Economics and Statistics, NITI Aayog and officers of the National Statistics Office (NSO), MoSPI.
The Report of the Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts presents the deliberations and recommendations for improving the methodology for compilation of State Domestic Product estimates under all three approaches, namely, the
Production Approach, Income Approach and Expenditure Approach
, as well as the methodology for compilation of District Domestic Product (DDP) estimates.
Major Methodological Improvements
includes:
Shift from allocation-based methods to direct estimation for some sectors or sub-sectors.
Reduction in reliance on fixed ratios and proxies.
Improved use of State-wise information of economic activity.
Greater methodological consistency across States.
The Uniform Guidelines for Compilation of Gross State Value Added (GSVA) under the Production Approach, as well as the Guidelines for Compilation of District Domestic Product (DDP), were uploaded on MoSPI’s website on 18.09.2026 and 03.06.2026, respectively, after incorporating suggestions received from stakeholders.
Further, the Draft Guidelines for Compilation of Gross State Value Added (GSVA) under the Expenditure Approach were uploaded on MoSPI’s website on 09.10.2026, inviting comments and suggestions from stakeholders by 28.10.2026. The final guidelines will be uploaded shortly after incorporating the suggestions received.
The Report is expected to serve as an important reference document for State and Union Territory Directorates of Economics and Statistics (DES) in strengthening their systems for compilation of State and District Domestic Product estimates under the revised base year series (2022–23).
The Report of the Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts is available on the official website of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation at
https://mospi.gov.in/uploads/documents/ReportSubCommitteeOnRegionalAccounts.pdf

subtitle:
Union Minister Smt. Annpurna Devi addressed the national campaign on Gender Equality and Women Empowerment on 25 November 2026

#NumberSaveKiya? campaign urged every woman to save Women Helpline 181 and Emergency 112 on her phone

MoWCD, DoJ, NALSA and DoRD signed Joint MoU on the Violence-Free Village Initiative
ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
date:

content:
The Ministry of Women and Child Development joined the Ministry of Rural Development for the inauguration of
Nayi Chetna 5.0
, the National Campaign on Gender Equality and Women Empowerment, on 25 November 2026 at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, PUSA, New Delhi. The event coincided with the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women and the start of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence.
The national event was graced by Smt. Annpurna Devi, Union Minister of Women and Child Development, along with Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister of Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare.
The Secretaries of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Department of Justice and the Department of Rural Development also attended the event.
Key announcements
Advisory on the 16 Days campaign:
The dignitaries released a Joint advisory issued by 10 Ministries and NALSA, guiding States and Union Territories to spread awareness, open access to support and legal aid, make women's safety everyone's responsibility, with the theme ‘From awareness to action & From access to agency’.
#NumberSaveKiya? Campaign:
Built around one simple question, “Number save kiya?” (Have you saved the number?), the campaign video urged every woman, and those around her, to save the Women Helpline 181 and Emergency Response Support System 112 on their phones. Helpline 181 is a 24x7, toll-free service, linking women facing violence to police, One Stop Centres, medical care and legal aid. The campaign will be amplified through the Ministry’s digital platforms and its grassroots network of Anganwadi workers, One Stop Centres and Mission Shakti hubs.
Addressing the gathering, Smt. Annpurna Devi launched the #NumberSaveKiya? campaign and the Helpline Anthem, and urged everyone to save the Women Helpline 181, Emergency Helpline 112 and Child Helpline 1098 on their phones and to spread awareness among others. She said, “In this digital age, the mobile phone has become a great companion. In times of distress, a woman can get immediate help with just one call to a One Stop Centre, Gender Resource Centre or the Women Helpline near her. But sometimes, under extreme stress, she may not remember the number, and help may be delayed. Knowing the right information and the right contact number at the time of need can be the first step towards handling even the biggest difficulty. Our message through this campaign is: know the number, save the number and share it with others. I would like to ask each one of you, ‘Number save kiya?’”
Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan affirmed that women’s empowerment, dignity and respect lie at the heart of the vision of Viksit Bharat, and lauded the contribution of nearly 3.75 crore Lakhpati Didis to the rural economy. Asserting that economic independence must go hand in hand with dignity, safety and equal opportunity, he called for collective effort to challenge patriarchal mindsets. Describing the MoU as a framework that brings safety, justice, rehabilitation and livelihood support together, he urged States, SHGs, Anganwadi networks and communities to turn the campaign into sustained grassroots action and to integrate the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan towards drug-free and violence-free villages. He also encouraged everyone to save the Women Helpline 181 and Emergency Helpline 112 on their phones.
Inter-Ministerial MoU:
An Inter-Ministerial MoU was signed by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Department of Justice, NALSA and Department of Rural Development to launch the Violence-Free Village Initiative, bringing legal aid, women’s support services and community institutions together at the village level.
Convergence on the ground
The morning sessions featured two panel discussions: one on ministerial convergence through Gender Resource Centres, One Stop Centres, the Legal Services Authority and the health system, and another with women leaders from the field. New Gender Resource Centres were launched, and SHG leaders and One Stop Centre administrators shared their experiences. The event also saw the release of video resources and the Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report, and the launch of the Nayi Chetna 5.0 Campaign.
As a part of Nayi Chetna 5.0, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, through its ‘Mission Shakti’, reaffirmed its commitment to the safety, security and empowerment of every woman.

content:
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister for Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, and Smt. Annapurna Devi, Union Minister for Women and Child Development, today launched the fifth edition of “Nayi Chetna: Pahal Badlaav Ki”, the National Campaign on Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment, at NASC Complex, PUSA, New Delhi. Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development; Shri Anil Malik, Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development; and Shri Niraj Verma, Secretary, Department of Justice, were present, along with senior officials of participating Ministries, State Governments, development partners and women leaders from across the country.
The centrepiece of the event was a landmark Quadripartite MoU on the Violence-Free Village Initiative (VFVI), signed by the Department of Rural Development, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Department of Justice and the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The MoU links DAY-NRLM’s Gender Resource Centres with One Stop Centres, Women Helpline 181, Disha 2.0 and legal aid services into a single chain of support, from prevention and protection to legal assistance and rehabilitation. To be piloted in 9 States and Union Territories, it rests on a simple promise: no woman facing violence should be left to find her way to help alone.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan affirmed that women’s empowerment, dignity and respect lie at the heart of the vision of Viksit Bharat, and lauded the contribution of nearly 3.75 crore Lakhpati Didis to the rural economy. Asserting that economic independence must go hand in hand with dignity, safety and equal opportunity, he called for collective effort to challenge patriarchal mindsets. Describing the MoU as a framework that brings safety, justice, rehabilitation and livelihood support together, he urged States, SHGs, Anganwadi networks and communities to turn the campaign into sustained grassroots action and to integrate the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan towards drug-free and violence-free villages.
Smt. Annapurna Devi highlighted the role of community institutions in taking the campaign to every household. Calling for wider use of support services, she urged citizens to remember, save and share Women Helpline 181 and Emergency Response Number 112, so that no woman in distress goes without timely help.
Shri Rohit Kansal traced Nayi Chetna’s journey from an awareness campaign to a nationwide, community-led movement, with 5.3 crore participants and nearly 7,000 Gender Resource Centres established so far. The fifth edition, he said, will turn that awareness and community trust into effective support, legal assistance and timely access to justice.
Shri Anil Malik called for seamless convergence of helplines, legal services and support institutions, backed by timely response and consistent follow-up. Highlighting the 16-day action agenda, he underlined the collective responsibility of families, communities and institutions towards women’s safety.
Shri Niraj Verma stressed the need to turn existing legal safeguards into services women can actually reach, particularly in rural and remote areas. He highlighted the role of NALSA, Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu, paralegal volunteers and Gender Resource Centres in strengthening legal awareness, referrals and free legal aid.
An Inter-Ministerial Joint Advisory was also unveiled, extending the Whole-of-Government approach to address gender-based discrimination and violence and advance women’s economic empowerment. The collaborating Ministries/Departments are: Rural Development, Women and Child Development; School Education and Literacy; Home Affairs; Panchayati Raj; Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Social Justice and Empowerment; Youth Affairs and Sports; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises; Information and Broadcasting; Justice; Labour and Employment; Revenue; and Road Transport and Highways.
Led by DAY-NRLM, the campaign will run across all States and Union Territories until 23 December 2026, built around four themes: Identity, Assetization, Mobility, and Redistribution of Unpaid Care Work. Through Self-Help Groups and community institutions, it will reach rural India with awareness drives, rallies, community meetings, street plays and dialogues with men and youth.
The event also saw the release of the Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report and the Nayi Chetna Anthem, and Gender Champions and One Stop Centre administrators shared experiences from the field. SHG women, Anganwadi workers, State Rural Livelihoods Missions and civil society partners took part in large numbers, reaffirming Nayi Chetna as a true Jan Andolan for gender equality.

title: National Milk Day
subtitle: “Celebrating India's Dairy Strength and Farmer Prosperity”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 10:55AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Milk at the Heart of India's Nutrition and Rural Economy
Milk occupies a vital place in India's nutritional landscape. It provides high-quality animal protein and essential nutrients, including calcium, magnesium and potassium, in easily absorbable forms. Often regarded as a near-complete food, milk supports growth, bone health and vitality across all age groups.
India has consistently remained the
world's largest milk producer
, contributing nearly
one-fourth of global milk production
. Between 2014-15 and 2024-25, production grew at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of
5.41 percent
, reaching
247.87 million tonnes
. This growth also has a significant rural dimension. Dairying provides livelihoods to
8.5 crore rural households
, with women playing a central role in milk production and collection. Nearly
70 percent of India’s dairy farming workforce comprises women
, highlighting their contribution to the sector's growth and its role in promoting inclusive rural development.
Observed every year on
26 November
,
National Milk Day
commemorates the birth anniversary of
Dr. Verghese Kurien
, the Father of India's White Revolution. The day recognises his transformative contribution to India's dairy cooperative movement. It honours the millions of dairy farmers whose efforts sustain the country's leadership in milk production.
India's Dairy Sector Records Strong Growth
India has maintained its position as the world's largest milk producer, supported by sustained growth in production and productivity.
Milk production
increased by
69.41 percent,
rising from
146.31 million tonnes in 2014-15
to
247.87 million tonnes in 2024-25
.
Leading milk-producing States
were Uttar Pradesh (
15.66 percent
), Rajasthan (14.82 percent), Madhya Pradesh (9.12 percent), Gujarat (7.78 percent), and Maharashtra (6.71 percent). These five States accounted for
54.09 percent
of total Milk production in the country.
Per capita milk availability
rose by
52.03 percent
, from
319 grams per person per day
in 2014-15
to
485 grams in 2024-25
.
Average bovine milk productivity
increased from
1,640 kilograms per animal per year in 2014-15
to
2,800 kg per animal per year in 2024-25
, registering growth of
69 percent.
The Cooperative Strength Behind India's Milk Economy
India's dairy cooperative movement provides an organised platform for milk producers. It connects village-level societies with district milk unions and State federations. These institutions support milk procurement, processing, marketing, and access to dairy services.
To explore the historical journey of India's dairy sector:
Click Here
The country's dairy cooperative network comprises:
22
milk federations.
241
district cooperative milk unions.
28
marketing dairies.
25
Milk Producer Organisations.
Coverage of approximately
2.45 lakh
villages and
1.65 crore
dairy farmers as members.
The network provides an institutional link between rural milk producers and organised dairy markets. It also supports collective marketing and access to better organised milk procurement systems.
NDDB Dairy Services
The National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)
has played an important role in developing farmer-owned dairy institutions in India. Its wholly owned, not-for-profit subsidiary,
NDDB Dairy Services (NDDB-DS)
, facilitates the incorporation and operationalisation of
Milk Producer Organisations (MPOs).
MPOs are farmer-owned Producer Companies that organise milk producers into professionally managed institutions. They facilitate collective milk procurement, strengthen market linkages, and provide farmers access to transparent pricing and direct bank payments.
As of 31 October 2026,
NDDB-DS has successfully established
25 MPOs
.
18 of these 25 MPOs
have all-women membership, with women serving as all the producer directors on their respective boards.
These organisations cover
more than 13 lakh milk producers
across
175 districts in 12 States
.
Women constitute around
78 percent
of the producers in these organisations.
The MPOs procure around
70 lakh litres of milk per day
.
Milk Procurement and Sales by Dairy Cooperatives
Dairy cooperatives provide an organised market for farmers and help ensure regular procurement of milk. Procurement prices are decided by the cooperatives and other dairies, based on production costs and market conditions. Many dairy cooperatives use automated milk collection and payment systems. Payments are credited directly to farmers' bank accounts.
As on 31 October 2026
, dairy cooperatives recorded:
690.90 lakh kg per day
of milk procurement.
462.95 lakh litres
per day
of liquid milk sales.
A New Momentum for Dairy Cooperatives
White Revolution 2.0,
a cooperative-led initiative formally launched on 25 December 2024 (SOP launched on 19 September 2024) aims to expand dairy cooperative coverage in uncovered villages and Panchayats. It seeks to increase milk procurement by dairy cooperatives by
50 percent
over the next five years. The initiative focuses on strengthening the cooperative network, improving market access, generating employment, and promoting women's empowerment. The activities envisaged under White Revolution 2.0 are funded under the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD).
By 2028-29, the initiative aims to establish
75,000 new Dairy Cooperative Societies
in uncovered villages and Panchayats and strengthen
46,422 existing Dairy Cooperative Societies
.
Progress under White Revolution 2.0
as
on 31 October 2026,
24,097
new Dairy Cooperative Societies formed.
31,394
existing Dairy Cooperative Societies strengthened.
Sustainability and Circularity in Dairy Sector
White Revolution 2.0
promotes sustainability and circularity across the dairy value chain. It encourages climate-smart practices, efficient resource utilisation and renewable, low-emission solutions. The initiative advances the vision of
‘Gold out of Garbage’ (
converting cattle dung and agricultural residues into biogas, organic manure, and value-added bio-fertilizers
)
through two Multi-State Cooperative Societies:
Cooperative Inputs and Services Delivery Multi-State Limited:
It aims to provide quality inputs and services, including animal feed, disease control, and artificial insemination.
Gomay Sahkari Samiti Multi-State Limited:
It focuses on the scientific management and utilisation of cattle dung.
GOBARdhan, the
National Circular Bioenergy Scheme
, launched on 01 October 2026, aims to
transform India's organic wealth into clean energy, rural prosperity and economic growth
. With an outlay of
Rs.
23,731 crore
, the scheme will be implemented from
FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36
.
It seeks to scale up domestic Compressed Biogas (CBG) production
nearly ten-fold
through assured offtake, stable pricing, capital assistance, pipeline connectivity and credit support. It will strengthen
energy security, mobilise private investment and promote a circular bioeconomy
.
The
Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan (GOBARdhan)
initiative was originally launched in 2018 under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen). It promotes converting organic waste, including cattle dung and agricultural residues, into biogas and bio-slurry, supporting village cleanliness, waste management, and rural livelihoods.
These initiatives strengthen resource circularity and create livelihood opportunities for rural households.
Building a Stronger Dairy Ecosystem
India's dairy sector relies on strong infrastructure, scientific breeding, quality feed and accessible veterinary care. Government initiatives strengthen these areas, improve livestock productivity, protect animal health and enhance returns to dairy farmers.
Strengthening Dairy Infrastructure through NPDD
The National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD)
seeks to enhance milk production and strengthen dairy infrastructure across the country. It supports milk procurement, processing, value addition, marketing, and milk quality infrastructure.
The programme promotes balanced growth of the dairy sector through
two components
:
Component A: Strengthening Milk Procurement and Quality Infrastructure
Focuses on expanding organised milk procurement networks, strengthening milk processing and value addition infrastructure in the North Eastern Region, hilly areas and Union Territories. It also supports village-level cold chains, milk testing facilities, and training on quality and clean milk production.
Component B: Dairying through Cooperatives
Seeks to increase milk and dairy product sales by improving farmers' access to organised markets. It supports dairy processing and marketing infrastructure and strengthens producer-owned institutions to improve farmers' returns.
Component B is implemented in nine States: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal.
NPDD’s Physical achievements as on 31 October 2026
40,800 new Dairy Cooperative Societies organised/revived.
25.82 lakh additional farmers enrolled with 161.17 lakh additional milk procurement
168 lakh litres per day
of milk chilling capacity created.
94,000 milk quality testing devices distributed
.
Rashtriya Gokul Mission
Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM)
has been initiated in December 2014 exclusively for development and conservation of indigenous bovine breeds in a scientific holistic manner. The scheme is playing important role in enhancing milk production and productivity of bovines to meet growing demand of milk and making dairying more remunerative to the rural farmers of the country. Revised in March 2025, the scheme emphasis on strengthening breeding infrastructure and expanding access to advanced reproductive technologies. Its interventions include strengthening semen stations, expanding artificial insemination services, and accelerating breed improvement through advance technologies such as sex-sorted semen & IVF technology.
Progress under RGM,
50,023
Multi-Purpose Artificial Insemination Technicians in Rural India (MAITRIs) trained & equipped.
24
In-Vitro Fertilization (IVF) laboratories established.
48
semen stations are being strengthened.
32
heifer rearing centres sanctioned.
Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme (NAIP)
The programme aims at enhancing Artificial Insemination coverage and delivering quality Artificial Insemination Services at farmer’s doorstep with semen of high genetic merit bulls including indigenous breeds.
Over 18.71 crore
artificial inseminations performed.
Nearly 11.17 crore
Animals covered.
Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)
The Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)
supports modern dairy processing, value addition and cold-chain infrastructure in the private sector and cooperatives.
It provides
3 percent interest subvention
to eligible beneficiaries for 8 years.
Through AHIDF 258 Dairy processing plants for the private sector and cooperatives have been supported with 3 percent interest subvention since 2020-21. This has leveraged investment of approx.
Rs. 21,797 crores.
Projects are approved with
500.58 lakh liters per day of
milk processing capacity and value-addition capacity.
Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme
The Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP)
supports prevention and control of economically important livestock diseases. It also strengthens veterinary infrastructure and provides doorstep veterinary services through Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs).
As of 31 October 2026,
4,019 MVUs
were operational across 29 States and Union Territories.
These units have provided doorstep services to
around
1
.5 crore
farmers
and treated
around 3.3 crore
animals.
National Animal Disease Control Programme
The National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP),
a component of LHDCP, supports Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) control and eventual eradication, alongside Brucellosis control through vaccination and surveillance.
As of 31 October 2026,
Cumulative FMD vaccination reached more than
1
52
crore doses
, benefiting around
8
crore farmers
.
FMD outbreaks declined from 132 in 2019 to 40 in 2025.
Brucellosis outbreaks declined from 22 in 2019 to 15 in 2025.
Digital Livestock Records through Bharat Pashudhan
The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, in collaboration with the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), has developed the
“Bharat Pashudhan”
database. Animals registered in the Bharat Pashudhan database are identified through a unique 12-digit ear-tag number, known as
“
Pashu Aadhaar”
.
It acts as a primary key for registering all types of transactions done on the animals, such as Vaccination, Breeding, Treatment, etc. The database provides a digital record of identified animals and supports livestock management.
As of 31 October 2026,
9,98,55,955
livestock owners have been registered.
Over
39.42 Crore
Pashu Aadhaar have been issued.
Indian Dairy Products in Global Markets
India’s dairy sector serves a large domestic market and is also expanding its presence internationally.
India exported
97,524.82 MT
of dairy products during 2025-26.
Export earnings reached
USD 407.12 million
during the year.
Major export destinations included the
UAE, Saudi Arabia, the USA, Bhutan, and Bahrain
.
These exports reflect the reach of India's dairy products across diverse international markets, extending the sector's presence beyond domestic consumption.
The Strength Behind Every Drop
India's dairy journey reflects the contribution of millions of farmers, women and cooperative institutions. Rising milk production, stronger infrastructure, scientific breeding and improved animal healthcare continue to support the sector's development. National Milk Day honours Dr. Verghese Kurien's legacy and recognises the farmers whose efforts sustain India's dairy leadership, strengthen rural livelihoods and contribute to the nation's nutritional security.

title: Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0
subtitle: Thirukkural Payilvom: Taking the Thirukkural to Campuses Across India
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 9:41AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Kashi Tamil Sangamam celebrates the longstanding cultural, linguistic and civilisational ties between Tamil Nadu and Kashi (Varanasi), reflecting the spirit of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat. The fifth edition, scheduled from 28 November to 12 December 2026, will focus on the theme
“Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”
, promoting the timeless teachings of the Thirukkural among young learners. Around 1,400 delegates from Tamil Nadu will visit Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya. A nationwide Students’ Engagement Programme will involve 1,000 Higher Education Institutions, while teachers from Tamil Nadu will introduce the Thirukkural in schools and colleges in Uttar Pradesh. Through academic exchanges, cultural programmes and multilingual outreach, the initiative seeks to deepen mutual understanding, strengthen people-to-people connections and promote India’s shared heritage.
About Kashi Tamil Sangamam
Kashi Tamil Sangamam celebrates the age-old civilisational bonds between Tamil Nadu and Kashi, the two ancient seats of learning. Many people from the two states have visited Kashi and Rameswaram as part of their religious traditions, reflecting the cultural bonds between the northern and southern parts of India.
Many people from Tamil Nadu have lived around Hanuman Ghat and Kedar Ghat for generations. Swami Kumaragurupara of Dharmapuram Adheenam came to Kashi from Tamil Nadu and built the Kedareshwar Temple at Kedar Ghat. The 200-year-old Kumaraswamy Mutt and Markandeya Ashram are situated at the same ghat. Tenkasi in Tamil Nadu is called the Kashi of the South. Banaras Hindu University has a chair dedicated to Mahakavi Subramania Bharati.
The broader objective of the Sangamam, set out when it was announced in 2022, is to bring the two knowledge and cultural traditions closer, create an understanding of shared heritage and deepen the people-to-people bond between the regions.
The first Kashi Tamil Sangamam was held in 2022, during Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav. Over its four editions, it has facilitated exchanges of knowledge, language, traditions and lived experiences between the two regions. The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, has called it a "vibrant programme which deepens the spirit of 'Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat'".
In each edition, students, teachers, artisans, scholars, spiritual leaders and cultural practitioners from Tamil Nadu have spent a week to ten days in Kashi. They have visited the temples of Kashi, places with Tamil links and the nearby cities of Ayodhya and Prayagraj. The participants also met their Kashi counterparts at seminars, talks, cultural programmes, sporting events and exhibitions.
The Sangamam is organised by the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, in collaboration with IIT Madras, Banaras Hindu University, the Central Institute of Classical Tamil (CICT), Chennai, and the Government of Uttar Pradesh. Several Central Ministries and Departments are also partners, among them Culture, Railways, Tourism and Textiles.
Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0: Thirukkural Payilvom
The fifth edition of the Sangamam will be held from 28 November to 12 December 2026 on the theme
"Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen"
(Let's Learn Thirukkural).
The Thirukkural is the classical Tamil text of ethics and conduct. Its author, Thiruvalluvar, set it in three parts:
Aram (virtue)
,
Porul (wealth)
, and
Inbam (love)
. The text has
1,330 couplets
, and CICT has translated it into 25 Indian languages including all 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution, in addition to several foreign languages and braille.
The aims of the fifth edition are:
•    To bring the ethical and moral wisdom of the Thirukkural closer to the youth and to learners across the country.
•    To encourage the reading, understanding and application of the values of the text in everyday life, through educational engagement, multilingual resources and wider public outreach.
•    To promote wider understanding of the Thirukkural among students from diverse academic disciplines and linguistic backgrounds.
Key Initiatives of Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0
Students' Engagement Programme
A nationwide Students' Engagement Programme will be undertaken through 1,000 Higher Education Institutions to promote wider understanding of the Thirukkural among students from diverse academic disciplines and linguistic backgrounds. It will include structured study, research and campus-based activities.
•Each participating institution will assess its interested students on the Thirukkural and nominate one student on merit.
•The selected students will attend an online academic orientation, offered in the 22 scheduled languages and in English.
•A one-month research and academic engagement will follow, with multilingual study material from CICT. Each eligible selected student will be entitled to a stipend of ₹10,000, subject to the programme guidelines and completion of the prescribed requirements.
•Each student will write an article or research note of 4 to 10 pages under a faculty guide, and give a one-hour presentation on the Thirukkural at the institution.
Thirukkural Teaching in Schools and Colleges of Uttar Pradesh
During the Sangamam, 50 teachers from Tamil Nadu will visit Uttar Pradesh and teach the Thirukkural in schools and colleges. Thirukkural experts from Tamil Nadu will also visit schools and colleges in Varanasi. They will introduce students to the core values of the text through orientation modules, interactive sessions and quizzes.
Reading Sessions in Schools
The National Book Trust, in association with the Rashtriya e-Pustakalaya, will conduct interactive sessions in schools in Varanasi on reading habits, storytelling and creative activities.
Inauguration, Conference and Cultural Programme
Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 will be inaugurated on 28 November 2026, and its valedictory function will be held on 12 December 2026. The students selected under the Students' Engagement Programme will join both functions online. Banaras Hindu University will co-host a National Conference on the Thirukkural, with the Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti as a partner. The Ministry of Culture will provide cultural troupes, screenings of the Thirukkural short films and cultural showcases at the venues. Handicraft and handloom outlets from Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh will be set up for the delegates at the main venue.
Digital and Public Outreach
Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 will also use technology to make the teachings of the Thirukkural accessible to a wider audience across India. The Thirukkural Multilingual App of CICT carries all 1,330 couplets with translations into the 22 scheduled languages. CICT's programme for the edition also includes short animated videos and films on selected couplets, and Thirukkural audiobooks. Couplets with translations are planned for passenger information systems and signboards at railway stations, airports and highway toll plazas, in coordination with Indian Railways, the Airports Authority of India and the National Highways Authority of India.
Delegates and Itinerary
Around
1,400 participants
from Tamil Nadu, organised into seven groups of around 200 persons each, will undertake an eight-day journey. It comprises four days of travel and four days of visits and structured programmes. The itinerary covers Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya, with cultural, academic, domain-specific and spiritual engagements.
The participants come from seven categories:
•    Students
•    Teachers
•    Writers and Media Professionals
•    Agriculture and Allied Sectors
•    Professionals and Artisans
•    Women
•    Spiritual leaders
During their stay in Varanasi, delegates will visit prominent religious, historical and cultural sites, including Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Sarnath or BHU, Ramnagar Fort and Bharat Mata Temple. The itinerary also includes Ganga Aarti, Ganga Snan, academic sessions and cultural programmes. Delegates will subsequently visit the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj and Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya.
A special Tamil heritage circuit will take delegates to Mahakavi Subramania Bharati’s ancestral house, Kedar Ghat and
Kashi Madam
in
Little Tamil Nadu
, along with an academic interaction at BHU’s Tamil Department.
Earlier Editions
The first four editions of Kashi Tamil Sangamam, held between 2022 and 2025, strengthened cultural, linguistic and historical ties between Tamil Nadu and Kashi. Building on this legacy, the fifth edition seeks to further deepen people-to-people connections and celebrate the shared heritage of the two regions.
Kashi Tamil Sangamam 1.0 (November to December 2022)
The first edition was held from November to December 2022. Over 2,500 people from Tamil Nadu, representing 12 different walks of life, travelled to Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya on eight-day tours. The event was organised at BHU, Varanasi. The Prime Minister inaugurated it at Varanasi on 19 November 2022. The delegates took part in seminars and site visits to meet people of similar trades, professions and interests. A month-long exhibition of handlooms, handicrafts, One District One Product items, books, documentaries, cuisine and art forms of the two regions was put up in Kashi, alongside academic exchanges, seminars and discussions between experts and scholars.
Kashi Tamil Sangamam 2.0 (December 2023)
The second edition was held from 17 to 30 December 2023 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi, and was inaugurated by the Prime Minister. It featured the first real-time, app-based translation of the Prime Minister's speech into Tamil for the visiting delegates. The programme for the edition provided for eight-day tours of Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya by train. The delegates were to travel in seven groups, each named after a sacred river such as the Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati, Sindhu, Narmada, Godavari and Cauvery. It included stalls of the art, handlooms, handicrafts and cuisine of Tamil Nadu and Kashi, cultural programmes at Namo Ghat, and academic exchanges on literature, ancient texts, philosophy, spirituality, music, dance, drama, yoga, Ayurveda and modern innovations.
Kashi Tamil Sangamam 3.0 (February 2025)
The third edition took place from 15 to 24 February 2025. It highlighted the legacy of Sage Agasthyar and linked the Indian knowledge tradition with contemporary discourse. Around 1,000 delegates from Tamil Nadu took part, along with an additional 200 students from various Central Universities. The programme for the edition included, for the first time, a visit to the Mahakumbh at Prayagraj and to the newly inaugurated Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. An exhibition on Sage Agasthyar, with seminars, workshops and book releases on his scholarly work, was planned in Kashi. The edition was in line with the emphasis of the National Education Policy 2020 on integrating Indian Knowledge Systems with modern systems of knowledge. The edition featured performances by over 869 artists and 190 local folk and classical groups, and drew nearly 2 lakh visitors.
Kashi Tamil Sangamam 4.0 (December 2025)
The fourth edition, held from 2 to 15 December 2025, focused on the theme
“Tamil Karkalam - Let us learn Tamil”
. It brought together over
1,400 delegates
from Tamil Nadu across seven categories. A key highlight was the arrival of 50 trained Tamil teachers and coordinators in Varanasi to teach basic Tamil to more than
1,500 students across 50 schools.
Under the
Tamil Karpom initiative
, Tamil learning study tours to Tamil Nadu were held for 300 college students from Kashi. The edition also featured the
Sage Agastya Vehicle Expedition
from Tenkasi to Kashi, highlighting the shared cultural and civilisational heritage of the two regions. Indian Railways operated seven special trains for delegates, while translations of the ancient Tamil text
Tolkappiyam
into four Indian and six foreign languages were released. The edition concluded with a valedictory function at Rameswaram on 30 December 2025.
Carrying Forward a Shared Civilisational Legacy
Kashi Tamil Sangamam reflects India's longstanding tradition of cultural exchange, where language, literature, knowledge and shared practices have connected communities across regions. By bringing people together through direct interaction and learning, the initiative seeks to deepen mutual understanding and strengthen the bonds between Tamil Nadu and Kashi.
With its focus on the
Thirukkural
, the fifth edition extends this engagement beyond the traditional setting of the Sangamam to educational institutions and young learners across the country. By encouraging the study of a classical Tamil text across linguistic and regional boundaries, it seeks to make India's literary and philosophical heritage more accessible to a wider audience. In doing so, Kashi Tamil Sangamam continues to advance the spirit of
Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat
, fostering national integration through shared knowledge, cultural understanding and people-to-people connections.

title: Major Step by India Towards Self-Reliance in Urea Production; 6 New Plants Approved
subtitle:
6 New Urea Plants to be Set Up in the Country under the National Investment policy for Urea (NIPU)-2026; The Goal Is Self-Reliance in Urea Production

An Investment of ₹54,000 Crore, Domestic Urea Expansion Targets Self-Reliance
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Fertilizers
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 NOV 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Aligned with the Vision of
Atmanirbhar Bharat
of Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri. Narendra Modi, the Government of India has taken a decisive step toward strengthening agricultural resilience, ensuring fertilizer security, and achieving self-reliance (
Atmanirbharta
) in urea production. Approving 6 new urea plants in brownfield category under the national investment Policy for Urea (NIPU)-2026—with more projects to follow—the initiative focuses on self-reliance in urea manufacturing with an investment of approximately ₹54,000 crore.
Focus on 6 New brownfield Plants, Investment, and Self-Reliance:
Under the National investment Policy for Urea (NIPU)-2026, 6 key brownfield urea projects have been taken forward across public sector, private sector, and cooperative enterprises:
MFL-Madras (Chennai, Tamil Nadu):
A PSU brownfield project with an annual installed production capacity of 12.7 LMT to replace the existing unit, which is over 60 years old that incurs higher production costs, high energy consumption, and safety hazards. Old plant being non-efficient needs to be replaced.
NFL Nangal (Nangal, Punjab):
A PSU brownfield replacement of a legacy PSU plant, around 50-55 years old, with present production capacity of 4.73 LMT/annum by a modern unit with an annual installed production capacity of 12.7 LMT.
KFL-Shahjahanpur (Shahjahanpur, Uttar Pradesh):
A cooperative brownfield project (KRIBHCO) expanding the unit commissioned in 1995, with an annual installed production capacity of 12.7 LMT.
Matix-Panagarh (Panagarh, West Bengal):
A private brownfield project building with an annual installed production capacity of 12.7 LMT on an existing modern plant commissioned in 2017. So far, West Bengal has only one urea plant. New plant will support the requirement of the State.
CFCL Gadepan (Gadepan, Kota, Rajasthan):
A private brownfield project expanding at the complex operational since 1994, with an annual installed production capacity of 12.7 LMT.
IIPL-Jagdishpur (Jagdishpur, Uttar Pradesh):
A private brownfield project proposing a 12.7 LMT/annum capacity addition at the plant established in 1988.
Capitalizing on brownfield advantages—such as existing land, utilities, infrastructure, logistics, and technical manpower—will enable faster execution and cost efficiency, while additional projects in the pipeline will further advance self-reliance.
Connection to Aging Plants and Replacement:
Legacy urea units—such as MFL-Madras (over 60 years old) and NFL Nangal (around 50–55 years old)—face higher production costs, elevated energy consumption, and process-safety risks. For instance, Nangal operates at 6.498 Gcal/MT compared to the weighted industry average of 5.95 Gcal/MT and the New Energy Norm of 5 Gcal/MT. Replacing and modernizing aging, energy-intensive units through brownfield expansion addresses safety and efficiency challenges while sustaining domestic urea supply.
Impact Against Consumption and Import Reduction:
India's annual urea demand/consumption stands at around 400 LMT (Lakh Metric Tonnes). Domestic urea production increased from 225 LMT per annum in 2014–15 to a record 314.07 LMT in 2023–24 and stood at 293.30 LMT during 2025–26, while total indigenous Reassessed Capacity (RAC) rose from 207.54 LMTPA in 2014–15 to 269.42 LMTPA during 2026–27. With fresh capacity additions and expansion plans measured against an annual consumption of around 400 LMT, reliance on imported urea is set to decrease substantially, saving foreign exchange and strengthening domestic availability.
Poised to Unlock ₹54,000 Crore Investment
With each brownfield project estimated at a capital cost norm of around ₹9,000 crore, the 6 urea plants are poised to attract nearly ₹54,000 crore in fresh investment, advancing India toward self-reliance (
Atmanirbharta
) in urea production while generating employment. To strengthen investor confidence and project bankability, the framework pairs a balanced 12–16% Return on Equity (RoE) band—anchored by a 12% floor and a 16% ceiling—with a foreign exchange rate mitigation mechanism that normalizes exchange rates and converts into INR after four years based on prevailing rates. Coupled with brownfield advantages that deliver an estimated ₹225 crore in annual savings—or roughly ₹1,800 crore over eight years—these provisions enhance financial viability and drive sustained capital inflows into domestic fertilizer manufacturing.
Success of New Investment Policy (NIP)-2012 and Detailed Outlook of India's Urea Policies:
Announced on 2nd January 2013 and amended on 7th October 2014, New Investment Policy-2012 led to the setting up of 6 new urea manufacturing units—4 through Joint Venture Companies (JVC) of nominated PSUs (Ramagundam unit of RFCL in Telangana; and Gorakhpur, Sindri, and Barauni units of HURL in Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Bihar, respectively) and 2 by private companies (Panagarh unit of Matix Fertilizers in West Bengal and Gadepan-III unit of Chambal Fertilizers in Rajasthan). Each unit has a 12.7 LMTPA production capacity, together adding 76.2 LMTPA and raising total indigenous RAC from 207.54 LMTPA in 2014–15 to 269.42 LMTPA in 2026–27. In addition, two 12.7 LMTPA projects are under execution: Talcher Fertilizer Project (TFL) in Odisha via coal-gasification route (expected to complete by December 2027) and Assam Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals Company Limited (AVFCCL) at Namrup, Assam (announced on 19th March 2025).
